Anyone on GitHub can assume this role.

  Anyone            exact           No grant is placed with people who have no account anywhere.
  Anyone on GitHub  exact  grant 1  Anyone on GitHub can assume this role; no condition confines its tokens to one owner.
  A named outsider  exact           No grant is placed with a named outsider.
  Your pipelines    exact           No grant is confined to owners declared as yours.
  Your people       exact           No grant trusts a SAML provider declared as yours.

Each of these can narrow the rings and was not read: the organisation's resource control policies, the calling accounts' service control policies and this account's identity providers.

grant 1 of 1 · statement[0] "EnterpriseByName" · Allow · https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com · platform · exact
This role admits any token from token.actions.githubusercontent.com whose aud is sts.amazonaws.com, whose enterprise was not evaluated and whose sub matches repo:*, so the set shown is an upper bound.
The set shown is an upper bound, not the set: a token not excluded here may still be refused by AWS.

  1  the condition key "token.actions.githubusercontent.com:enterprise" is not one AWS documents for the tokens of "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com", so whether a request carries it is not known and the claim is not constrained
     caveat · enterprise · statement[0].Condition
  2  same as note 1

a token this grant admits
  {
    "iss": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
    "aud": "sts.amazonaws.com",

The decoded payload. A claim not shown and not named by the grant is unconstrained, but for azp; enterprise is not shown because it was not evaluated, so whether it excludes a token is not decided here. It sets no azp: AWS reads aud from azp whenever a token sets one.
